topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These framing remarks introduce the lecturer, outline the course structure, and establish the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic, Environmental, and Epidemiological Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental origins of cancer, contrasting intrinsic genetic mutations and stochastic risk with environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogenic and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents and viruses drive malignant transformation, focusing on cellular mechanisms and the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens: Metabolic Activation and DNA Adducts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical exposures undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Two-Stage Carcinogenesis, and Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, two-stage carcinogenesis models, and the role of developmental timing in cancer susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogens and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental and analytical strategies used to demonstrate carcinogenicity, including mutational signature profiling, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo assays, and the Ames test.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Assessment and Lecture Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding section discusses everyday risk-benefit trade-offs associated with carcinogen exposures and summarizes the lecture's key concepts.
